600	>> But as we said before, this moving mitzvah
601	that begins from the very moment you are in your field and see
602	the first fruit
603	and already feel the endearment toward it, and you mark
604	it throughout the whole continuation, with the colorful procession,
605	and with the arrival in Jerusalem and the bringing to the Beit HaMikdash,
606	up to the peak of "you shall speak and say before HaShem your Elokim",
607	this whole matter is in essence the most general theme,
608	which touches all generations and times, even in our times,
609	each and every one. Why?
610	So the Rebbe says, let us study a little the meaning of
611	the mitzvah of Bikurim. This special mitzvah
612	belongs, in its content, to a family, if one may
613	call it that, of mitzvot
614	that deal with praise and acknowledgment to HaShem, blessed be He.
615	That is, HaShem commands us in several
616	mitzvot in which we find the opportunity
617	to thank and to praise HaShem,
618	like blessings and prayers.
619	So too with the mitzvah of Bikurim. What is the idea,
620	that a Jew takes the first fruit of the earth and brings it to HaShem?
621	To show that he thanks HaShem for all the crops
622	and for all the produce that HaShem gave him?
623	>> To receive a blessing.
624	>> Now, this concept of gratitude is
625	a most fundamental concept
626	in human life, and even, by contrast, for a non-
627	Jew.
628	Every human being, if he has only human nature,
629	knows how to give thanks,
630	not to treat everything he receives from another as
631	taken for granted.
632	Even the nations of the world give thanks for their economy.
633	We know the point the Rebbe mentioned
634	many times, that on the dollar of the United States, what is
635	written?
636	>> Yes, "In God We Trust." That is, we know
637	that the economy comes from Him, and so it is praise and thanks
638	to HaShem. What does an elected president of the United States say
639	in his first presidential speech? How does he open?
640	What are his first words? Thank HaShem that I was elected.
641	They know how to thank HaShem.
642	All the more so, a fortiori, with the people of Israel. With the people of
643	Israel, thanks to HaShem is not only sometimes. Thanks
644	can also be a kind of... yes, it is written on
645	the dollar, but it is not certain that it is written in the heart.
646	It may be that it is the first sentence you say,
647	but it is not certain that it is the first sentence, that it is the sentence
648	that accompanies you throughout your whole term in office. Right?
649	In the Torah it accompanies us throughout all of life, every
650	day and all day. Every time you come to eat something,
651	the blessings over enjoyment. What are the blessings over enjoyment that the Sages instituted for us?
652	>> Every time you come to enjoy something from the world, whether
653	food, or a pleasant fragrance, or new clothing
654	or a new house, you always thank HaShem for the enjoyment.
655	So although all the individual blessings are rabbinic,
656	the blessing that is from the Torah, which is Birkat HaMazon,
657	is truly a Torah obligation: "And you shall eat, and be satisfied, and bless."
658	That is, a Jew, as we said before, throughout
659	his daily life, all his life, thanks HaShem.
660	He gets up in the morning, what is the first word he says
661	when he opens his eyes? "Modeh."
662	>> "Modeh ani lefanecha." We once told the moving story
663	of the Rebbe's mother, who managed to be saved from all
664	the suffering that there was under
665	the Communists, and arrived in the United States. So
666	uh,
667	she lived in Crown Heights, in the Rebbe's neighborhood,
668	and until 5725, which was in fact the year of her passing
669	(in Tishrei, soon, is her yahrtzeit), the Rebbe
670	came every day to visit his mother,
671	every day at exactly the same hour, truly like
672	a Swiss clock, for about half an hour, to visit
673	his mother, may her memory be a blessing.
674	And
675	someone took the opportunity, someone who was
676	a friend of the Rebbetzin, Rebbetzin Chana, and asked her
677	whether she could say what was the Rebbe's
678	favorite prayer.
679	So she did not know what to say, so she said, "I will
680	ask him." Now, the only one who can ask
681	the Rebbe such a thing and also be sure to get an answer is
682	his mother. So that is how it was. So what was the Rebbe's answer?
683	"Modeh ani lefanecha."
684	That is, this matter of simply opening
685	your eyes and saying thank you to HaShem is something so
686	essential in the life of a Jew that it accompanies the Jew
687	throughout the whole day.
688	[music]
689	And
690	so, the mitzvah of Bikurim is one more possibility
691	and way in which a Jew can express his gratitude to HaShem
692	for the produce that HaShem gave him. Except that if one pays
693	attention, one sees that in the mitzvah of Bikurim there is something
694	exceptional compared to all the other mitzvot of acknowledgment and praise
695	to HaShem, which makes it something unique in its kind.
696	And what is it? That in the mitzvah of Bikurim, thanks to HaShem is
697	not only in words,
698	it is in deeds.
699	HaShem gives us abundance in deeds, not
700	in words. Not only blessings, but this is all
701	what is called in actual practice. In deed and openly. How does a Jew
702	say thank you? Usually with the mouth. The novelty in the mitzvah of
703	Bikurim is that it is a mitzvah that takes all of you,
704	and in the fullest way, with speech and deed and thought.
705	You, in essence, this is the process we described earlier,
706	which continues for months, from the moment you tie
707	the sign on the fruit until the moment you find yourself
708	standing before HaShem your Elokim, and everyone is listening, "and you shall speak
709	and say before HaShem your Elokim."
710	And even in the simplest sense, you take the fruits
711	that are so dear to you and so
712	meaningful and precious to you, and leave them at home,
713	in the House of HaShem, you leave them to HaShem, blessed be He. You do not just
714	bring them and take them back home
715	with the holiness they absorbed; you leave them to HaShem.
716	That is, your thanks is in the fullest sense of the word
717	descending into actual reality; it finds
718	expression in deeds.
